MODIFIER_STACKING_WARNING.description: Modifier stacking uses TWO separate pools that never cross-apply. Prep tasks use condition_scale x door_type_complexity x height. Coating tasks use quality_tier x door_type_complexity x height. Contamination drives task activation, not rate modification.
MODIFIER_STACKING_WARNING.worst_case_prep: POOR(2.00) x louvered(2.50) x H2(1.30) = 6.50x — extremely rare combination, flag for estimator review
MODIFIER_STACKING_WARNING.worst_case_coating: QT5(1.80) x louvered(2.50) x H2(1.30) = 5.85x — louvered + QT5 unlikely, flag for review

prep_tasks.formula: effective_rate = base_rate / (condition_scale x door_type_complexity x height)

coating_tasks.formula: effective_rate = base_rate / (quality_tier x door_type_complexity x height)

task_production_rates.name: Floor Protection Setup (Perimeter Drops — Brush)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Drop cloth at each door location. ~5 min per opening. RP always has finished floors. Adapted from NC TSK_DOOR_FLOOR_PROTECT (12 EA/hr) — same task, same rate. Brush method uses perimeter drops only.

task_production_rates.name: Floor Protection Setup (8ft Radius — Spray)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Rosin paper 8ft radius per opening. ~10 min per opening. Adapted from NC TSK_DOOR_SPRAY_PROTECT (6 EA/hr). Spray overspray containment requires full coverage.

task_production_rates.name: Wall Masking Around Door Opening (Spray)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mask wall surfaces around door opening with tape and masking paper. ~7-8 min per opening (both sides). Adapted from NC TSK_FRAME_WALL_PROTECT_SPRAY (10 EA/hr) — RP slightly slower due to finished wall precision masking. RP walls are already painted; requires clean tape line.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Door Hardware (Spray)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove lockset + 3 hinges + strike plate, bag and label, remove door from frame. ~20 min per door. Direct transfer from NC TSK_DOOR_HARDWARE_REMOVE (3 EA/hr). RP hardware may have paint build-up making removal slightly slower — captured in range.

task_production_rates.name: Mask Door Hardware (Brush)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mask 3 hinge leaves + lockset + strike plate with tape. ~15 min per door. Adapted from NC TSK_DOOR_HARDWARE_MASK (4 EA/hr). Same rate — masking complexity identical for RP.

task_production_rates.name: Mask Glass Panes (French Doors)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tape all 4 edges of each glass pane. ~6 min per pane. Direct transfer from NC TSK_DOOR_GLASS_MASK (10 EA/hr). Same precision masking regardless of NC/RP.

task_production_rates.name: Visual Condition Scan — Frame + Slab Per Opening

QT3.notes: Standard visual with work light, document visible defects on frame and slab. ~7-8 min per opening.

QT4.notes: Systematic scan with raking light, photograph all defect areas, per-component assessment. ~10 min per opening.

QT5.notes: Critical assessment, multiple passes, raking light, full photographic documentation per component. ~15 min per opening.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP-new task. Combined frame + slab assessment per opening. Door assessment is more thorough than wall assessment (smaller surface, higher scrutiny). Rates calibrated against wall RP TSK_WLRP_ASSESS_CONDITION (15 min/room QT3 = ~4 walls). Door is ~1 opening with 2 components.

task_production_rates.name: Adhesion Test (ASTM D3359 Cross-Hatch Tape Test)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Cross-hatch tape test per ASTM D3359 at 2 locations per opening (1 frame + 1 slab). ~7-8 min per opening. Calibrated against wall RP TSK_WLRP_ASSESS_ADHESION (8 min fixed). Two test locations vs one for walls but smaller prep area.

task_production_rates.name: Coating Identification — Latex vs Oil
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Solvent rub test at 1 location per opening. ~5 min per opening. Faster than adhesion test — single rub with mineral spirits + observation. Doors historically oil-based, making this test critical for primer selection.

task_production_rates.name: Moisture Check — Frame Bottoms
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Moisture meter reading on frame bottoms. ~4 min per opening. Quick test — point meter at suspect areas, record reading. Only applicable for bathroom/kitchen/laundry doors but estimator includes for all openings to cover assessment time.

task_production_rates.name: Lead Test (XRF or Swab)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Lead test at 2 locations per opening (1 frame + 1 slab). ~10 min per opening with XRF, ~8 min with swab. Doors are HIGH RISK for lead paint. Shared RRP module task — rate consistent across interior RP specs.

task_production_rates.name: RRP Containment Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Install poly sheeting containment around door opening. ~15 min per opening. EPA RRP Rule 40 CFR 745. Shared RRP module task.

task_production_rates.name: HEPA Vacuum After Paint Disturbance
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: HEPA vacuum all surfaces after each sanding/scraping disturbance. ~7-8 min per opening per pass. Multiple passes may be needed. Shared RRP module task.

task_production_rates.name: RRP Containment Removal and Visual Clearance
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove containment poly, visual clearance inspection. ~10 min per opening. Shared RRP module task.

task_production_rates.name: Lead-Contaminated Waste Disposal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Package and dispose lead-contaminated debris per EPA RRP Rule. Fixed time per project regardless of door count. ~30 min. Shared RRP module task.

task_production_rates.name: TSP Wash Frame + Slab Surfaces
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: TSP wash frame and both slab sides per opening. ~10 min per opening. Wipe on, scrub detail areas, rinse, dry. RP-new task — no NC equivalent (new substrate is clean). Contamination-dependent activation.

task_production_rates.name: Mildew/Biocide Treatment
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply bleach/mildewcide solution, full contact time, rinse. ~15 min per opening including dwell time. RP-new task. Bathroom/kitchen door frames are common mildew locations.

task_production_rates.name: Degloss Door Frame Surfaces

QT3.notes: Chemical or mechanical degloss, all accessible frame surfaces. ~7-8 min per frame.

QT4.notes: Full degloss with adhesion verification on stop profile. ~10 min per frame.

QT5.notes: Complete degloss with verification and spot adhesion re-test. ~12 min per frame.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP replacement for NC TSK_FRAME_SAND_PREP (12 EA/hr). RP degloss is slower than NC sand prep — chemical degloss requires wipe-on, dwell, wipe-off vs simple scuff. Door stop profile areas need contour attention. Rates are QT3 baseline.

task_production_rates.name: Degloss Door Slab Surface

QT3.notes: Chemical or mechanical degloss, full face + edge. ~10 min per side.

QT4.notes: Full degloss with adhesion verification, panel recesses addressed. ~12 min per side.

QT5.notes: Complete degloss with verification, all panel detail areas. ~15 min per side.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP replacement for NC TSK_DOOR_SAND_PREP (8 EA_SIDE/hr). RP degloss is slower — chemical process vs simple scuff. Panel doors significantly slower due to crevice access. Flush door baseline. Door_type_complexity modifier applies to slab tasks.

task_production_rates.name: Scrape Loose Paint and Feather Edges — Frame + Slab

QT3.notes: Remove failing paint, feather edges — no visible ridge at 6 ft. ~15 min per side.

QT4.notes: Comprehensive scrape + near-invisible feathering at 3 ft. ~20 min per side.

QT5.notes: Critical scrape + perfect feathering — no ridge at arm's length. ~30 min per side.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP-new task — no NC equivalent (NC is bare wood, no existing paint to scrape). Labor-intensive on panel doors — contour scraper required. Combined scrape + feather. Non-negotiable feathering at all tiers — ridge telegraphing through fine-finish coats is unacceptable. FAIR baseline shown; POOR doubles the work.

task_production_rates.name: Assess and Replace Failed Caulk — Frame-to-Casing Joints

QT3.notes: Replace visibly failed sections. ~7-8 min per frame. ~15-20% joint replacement typical.

QT4.notes: Comprehensive assessment, replace all suspect + failed joints. ~10 min per frame.

QT5.notes: Replace all joints not in perfect condition, perfect tooled bead. ~15 min per frame.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Modified from NC TSK_FRAME_CAULK_CASING (10 EA/hr). RP is slower — assess existing, remove failed, apply new vs NC simple bead. NC = full new caulk on bare joint; RP = selective replacement. QT3 baseline assumes 15-20% joint replacement.

task_production_rates.name: Fill and Patch Damaged Areas — Frame + Slab

QT3.notes: Fill obvious damage and hardware change holes. ~7-8 min per opening.

QT4.notes: Fill all visible defects, careful feathering. ~10 min per opening.

QT5.notes: Fill every defect, near-zero tolerance, wood hardener where needed. ~15 min per opening.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Modified from NC TSK_FRAME_FILL_STOP_HOLES (20 EA/hr). RP fill/patch is significantly slower — damage-related defects vs routine nail holes. Combined frame + slab per opening. Includes wood hardener on moisture-softened frame bottoms.

task_production_rates.name: Sand Filled Areas Smooth
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Sand all filler spots flush on frame + slab per opening. ~5 min per opening. Adapted from NC TSK_FRAME_SAND_FILL (30 EA/hr frame only) + NC TSK_DOOR_SAND_FILL (30 EA_SIDE/hr). Combined task covers both components — more spots than NC but single pass per opening.

task_production_rates.name: Dust Wipe Frame + Slab Surfaces
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth wipe all frame + slab surfaces per opening. ~4 min per opening. Adapted from NC TSK_FRAME_CLEAN_DUST (40 EA/hr frame only) + NC TSK_DOOR_CLEAN_DUST (30 EA_SIDE/hr). Combined per-opening task covers both components.

task_production_rates.name: Brush State-Driven Primer on Frame
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush adhesion/stain-block/mildew primer on frame set. ~8-9 min per frame. Adapted from NC TSK_FRAME_PRIME_BRUSH (8 EA/hr). RP slightly slower — adhesion primers are thicker/tackier than standard primer, require careful application. Head jamb → side jambs → stop.

task_production_rates.name: Spray State-Driven Primer on Frame
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray state-driven primer on frame set. ~5 min per frame. Adapted from NC TSK_FRAME_PRIME_SPRAY (15 EA/hr). RP slightly slower — adhesion primers require adjusted pressure and slower pass speed. Spray rate MUST be faster than brush rate (12 > 7). CHECK: spray(12) > brush(7) — PASS.

task_production_rates.name: Brush State-Driven Primer on Slab
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush state-driven primer on slab face + edge. ~15 min per side. Adapted from NC TSK_DOOR_PRIME_BRUSH (5 EA_SIDE/hr). RP slightly slower — adhesion primers are tackier, require careful tip-off. Panel doors: panels first, rails, then stiles.

task_production_rates.name: Spray State-Driven Primer on Slab
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray state-driven primer on slab face + edge. ~6 min per side. Adapted from NC TSK_DOOR_PRIME_SPRAY (12 EA_SIDE/hr). RP slightly slower — adhesion primers need adjusted settings. Spray rate MUST be faster than brush rate (10 > 4). CHECK: spray(10) > brush(4) — PASS.

task_production_rates.name: Spot Prime Scraped/Repaired Areas

QT3.notes: Spot prime all repair areas. ~6 min per opening.

QT4.notes: Spot prime all repairs with feathered edges. ~7-8 min per opening.

QT5.notes: Spot prime all repairs with wide feather, may need light sand after. ~10 min per opening.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP-new task. Spot prime scraped, feathered, caulked, and patched areas to prevent flashing. Brush application regardless of method — spot work always brushed. GOOD condition has fewer spots; FAIR/POOR have more.

task_production_rates.name: Inspect Coat (Interstage) — Frame + Slab

QT3.notes: Quick glance at 6 feet — obvious defects only. ~4 min per opening.

QT4.notes: Systematic scan at 3 feet — mark all visible defects. ~6 min per opening.

QT5.notes: Lighted critical inspection at arm's length — zero tolerance. ~10 min per opening.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Combined frame + slab interstage inspection per opening. Adapted from NC TSK_FRAME_INSPECT_COAT (30 EA/hr) + NC TSK_DOOR_INSPECT_COAT (20 EA_SIDE/hr). Combined task slower per opening than either individual NC task — covers both components.

task_production_rates.name: Sand Between Coats — Frame

QT3.notes: Spot sand nibs 220 grit. ~4 min per frame.

QT4.notes: Full sand 220 grit, uniform scratch pattern. ~6 min per frame.

QT5.notes: Thorough 320 grit, every imperfection. ~7-8 min per frame.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Adapted from NC TSK_FRAME_LIGHT_SAND (12 EA/hr). RP interstage sanding on previously painted surfaces. QT3 is slightly faster than NC baseline (spot sand vs scuff). Contour sponge for door stop profile.

task_production_rates.name: Sand Between Coats — Slab

QT3.notes: Spot sand nibs 220 grit. ~6 min per side.

QT4.notes: Full sand 220 grit, uniform scratch pattern. ~10 min per side.

QT5.notes: Thorough 320 grit, every imperfection. ~12 min per side.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Adapted from NC TSK_DOOR_LIGHT_SAND (8 EA_SIDE/hr). RP interstage sanding. Panel doors significantly slower due to recess detail. Rigid sanding block mandatory for flat surfaces (FFD 15.4.1), contour sponge for recesses.

task_production_rates.name: Patch/Repair Defects (Interstage)

QT3.notes: Repair only glaring defects — deep scratches, obvious holes. ~4 min per opening.

QT4.notes: Repair all marked defects — visible at 3 feet. ~6 min per opening.

QT5.notes: Repair all defects regardless of size. ~10 min per opening.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Combined frame + slab interstage defect repair per opening. Adapted from NC TSK_FRAME_PATCH_REPAIR (30 EA/hr) + NC TSK_DOOR_PATCH_REPAIR (20 EA_SIDE/hr). RP has more defects to address than NC — existing paint issues add repair scope.

task_production_rates.name: Spot Coat Patched Areas

QT3.notes: Spot coat obvious repairs only. ~4 min per opening.

QT4.notes: Spot coat all patched areas. ~6 min per opening.

QT5.notes: Spot coat all repairs, ensure uniform film build. ~7-8 min per opening.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP-new task. Apply spot coat over patched/repaired areas on frame and slab to build film thickness. Brush application. Scope proportional to quality tier — QT5 requires more spot repairs to maintain zero-defect standard.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Sanding Dust (Interstage)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth wipe frame + slab between coats per opening. ~4 min per opening. Adapted from NC TSK_FRAME_CLEAN_INTERSTAGE (40 EA/hr) + NC TSK_DOOR_CLEAN_INTERSTAGE (30 EA_SIDE/hr). Combined per-opening task.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Finish Coat on Frame
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush finish coat on frame set. ~12 min per frame. Adapted from NC TSK_FRAME_FINISH_BRUSH (6 EA/hr). RP slightly slower — fine-finish enamel on previously painted surface requires more careful application to avoid lifting. Apply, tip once, walk away per FFD 15.3.1.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Finish Coat on Frame
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray finish coat on frame set. ~6 min per frame. Adapted from NC TSK_FRAME_FINISH_SPRAY (12 EA/hr). RP slightly slower — fine-finish enamel atomization requires adjusted settings on repainted surface. Spray rate MUST be faster than brush rate (10 > 5). CHECK: spray(10) > brush(5) — PASS.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Finish Coat on Slab
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush finish coat on slab face + edge. ~17 min per side. Adapted from NC TSK_DOOR_FINISH_BRUSH (4 EA_SIDE/hr). RP slightly slower — waterborne fine-finish enamel on previously painted surface demands careful first-pass technique, especially on panel doors. Apply, tip once, walk away per FFD 15.3.1.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Finish Coat on Slab
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray finish coat on slab face + edge. ~7-8 min per side. Adapted from NC TSK_DOOR_FINISH_SPRAY (10 EA_SIDE/hr). RP slightly slower — fine-finish enamel atomization on repainted surface. Spray rate MUST be faster than brush rate (8 > 3.5). CHECK: spray(8) > brush(3.5) — PASS.

task_production_rates.name: Roll and Tip Finish Coat on Frame
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roll and Tip method for frame flat surfaces. ~10 min per frame. Adapted from NC TSK_FRAME_FINISH_ROLL_TIP (7 EA/hr). RP slightly slower. Alternative to TSK_DIRP_FINISH_FRAME_BRUSH — estimator selects one or the other, not both. Roll and tip produces smoother finish than brush-only on flat jamb surfaces. Per FFD 15.6.

task_production_rates.name: Reinstall Door Hardware and Rehang Door (Spray)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Reinstall lockset + hinges, rehang door, verify operation. ~20 min per door. Adapted from NC TSK_DOOR_HARDWARE_REINSTALL (4 EA/hr). RP slightly slower — fresh fine-finish paint requires careful handling to avoid marring. Must verify no binding with new paint film build.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Hardware Masking (Brush)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove masking tape from hinges, lockset, strike plate. ~6 min per door. Adapted from NC TSK_DOOR_HARDWARE_UNMASK (12 EA/hr). RP slightly slower — more paint build-up at tape edge from RP coat sequence (primer + 2 finish vs NC 2 finish). Remove while slightly tacky for cleanest pull.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Glass Masking (French Doors)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove masking tape from each glass pane. ~4 min per pane. Adapted from NC TSK_DOOR_GLASS_UNMASK (20 EA/hr). RP slightly slower — more paint build-up at tape edge. Remove while slightly tacky for cleanest pull.

task_production_rates.name: Touch Up Hinge Mortise Areas
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Touch up 3 hinge mortises + 1 strike mortise after hardware reinstall. ~5 min per door. Adapted from NC TSK_FRAME_MORTISE_TOUCHUP (15 EA/hr). RP slightly slower — must blend with existing multi-coat build-up. Spray method only (brush method has hardware masked in place).

task_production_rates.name: Final Inspection — Frame + Slab

QT3.notes: Quick glance at 6 feet — no obvious defects, uniform sheen. ~6 min per opening.

QT4.notes: Systematic scan at 3 feet — no visible defects, verify door operation. ~10 min per opening.

QT5.notes: Critical inspection at arm's length under raking light — zero tolerance, gallery-quality. ~15 min per opening.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Combined frame + slab final inspection per opening. Adapted from NC TSK_FRAME_FINAL_INSPECT (30 EA/hr) + NC TSK_DOOR_FINAL_INSPECT (20 EA_SIDE/hr). RP final inspection includes verifying door operation, hardware installation, and finish quality on both components.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-Up Defects (Final)

QT3.notes: Address obvious defects only. ~6 min per opening.

QT4.notes: Address all visible defects, blend into surrounding finish. ~10 min per opening.

QT5.notes: Every imperfection — full coat over spot repairs if needed to equalize sheen. ~15 min per opening.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP-new task. Touch up remaining defects found during final inspection on frame and slab. Spot sand and recoat as needed. More touch-up scope in RP than NC — existing paint condition introduces more defect opportunities.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Wall Masking (Spray)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove tape and masking paper from walls around door opening. ~5 min per opening. Adapted from NC TSK_FRAME_WALL_PROTECT_TEARDOWN (20 EA/hr). RP slightly slower — finished wall requires careful tape removal to avoid pulling wall paint.

task_production_rates.name: Floor Protection Teardown
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove floor protection per opening. ~4 min per opening. Fold toward center to contain debris. Adapted from NC TSK_DOOR_FLOOR_PROTECT_TEARDOWN (20 EA/hr). RP slightly slower — more debris from scraping/sanding.

task_production_rates.name: Customer Walkthrough
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Walk each door with homeowner. ~7-8 min per door. RP-specific — occupied home context requires client sign-off. Inspect finish, verify door operation, check hardware, address touch-up requests on the spot. No NC equivalent.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Tools
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Clean brushes, spray equipment (if used), rollers. Fixed time per session regardless of door count. ~30 min. All waterborne products — water cleanup. Adapted from NC TSK_DOOR_CLEAN_TOOLS (same 30 min fixed).

quality_tier_effects.description: Standard door repaint — MINIMUM TIER for doors, baseline for all rates
quality_tier_effects.notes: QT3 is the MINIMUM acceptable tier for door slabs and frames. Per Doors Doctrine QT3 = 1.0. This is the floor — no cheaper option available for doors.

quality_tier_effects.description: Premium door repaint — thorough prep, full sand between coats, crisp edges
quality_tier_effects.notes: Per Doors Doctrine §6.1 QT4 labor factor = 1.4. DOOR-SPECIFIC higher modifier than global (1.3). Full sand 220 between coats. Systematic inspection. Applied to qt_scaled tasks only.

quality_tier_effects.description: Superior door repaint — maximum care, zero tolerance, 320-grit between coats, 3 brush coats per FFD 15.10.3
quality_tier_effects.notes: Per Doors Doctrine §6.1 QT5 labor factor = 1.8. DOOR-SPECIFIC higher modifier than global (1.5). Thorough sand 320 between coats. Critical inspection. QT5 brush adds 3rd finish coat per FFD 15.10.3. Applied to qt_scaled tasks only.

door_type_complexity.notes: Raised panel. Deeper recesses than flat panel.
French door. Glass masking is dominant labor. Per Doors Doctrine §9.2.
Bifold door panel. Smaller, simpler. Per Doors Doctrine §1.1.
Louvered door. Extreme complexity — individual slat painting. Spray-only for RP. Per Doors Doctrine §12.2.

frame_type_complexity.notes: Pocket door frame. No door stop. ~15% less surface.
Cased opening. Jambs only, no stop, no hardware. ~25% less work.
Bifold door frame. Track hardware instead of hinges. ~10% less work.

height_access_effects.notes: Tall openings 7'0"-8'0". Step ladder for head jamb.
High openings 8'0"+. Rare for interior. Scaffold may be needed.

condition_scale_effects.notes: Sound paint, adhesion passes, latex-over-latex compatible. Minimal prep.
Failing paint, localized peeling, some damage. Moderate prep. Scrape/feather + fill/patch activated.
Extensive peeling, moisture damage, smoke damage. Full prep. All condition-dependent tasks activated at maximum scope.

application_method_effects.description: Airless spray application — fastest coating but requires more setup (floor 8ft radius, wall mask, hardware remove)
application_method_effects.notes: Spray produces superior finish on doors. Production method for 10+ doors. Requires door removal and full containment.

application_method_effects.description: Brush application — less setup but slower coating. RP default for occupied homes with fewer doors.
application_method_effects.notes: Brush is default for RP (occupied home, 1-5 doors). Door stays hung, hardware masked. Roll-and-tip available for flat frame surfaces.

round_configurations.notes: Standard RP round with state-driven prime. Most common for doors with adhesion or contamination issues.
GOOD condition, skip prime. Sound paint with adhesion verified.
Maximum coat sequence. QT5 brush per FFD 15.10.3 + state-driven prime.
QT5 brush 3-coat finish sequence, no prime needed.

crew_configurations.name: Door RP Spray Crew
crew_configurations.notes: One journeyman sprayer handles all doors. Helper assists with masking/protection setup and teardown.

crew_configurations.name: Door RP Brush Painter
crew_configurations.notes: One journeyman brush painter. Roll-and-tip option for flat frame surfaces.

rate_validation_checks.rule: Spray rate MUST be >= brush rate on paired application tasks
No rates above 2000 for any unit
rate_validation_checks.notes: All rates are EA-based or FIXED. Maximum rate is 15 EA/hr.
All 50 tasks verified: rate_range_low < rate_per_hour < rate_range_high (or equivalent for rates_by_tier).

assumptions.value: RP tasks ~10-20% slower than equivalent NC tasks
assumptions.source: Previously painted surfaces are more difficult to work with — adhesion primers are thicker, existing paint can lift, scraping generates additional debris

assumptions.value: Assessment, fill/patch, dust wipe, interstage inspect, and cleanup tasks are combined per-opening (frame + slab together)
assumptions.source: Efficiency gain — painter works entire opening as unit rather than separate frame/slab passes
Resolution.json factor_modifiers, consistent with wall RP and trim RP specs
Doors Doctrine §6.1 — doors are scrutinized surfaces requiring higher QT differentiation
